name: Anthropic (demo)
tagline: A fictional slice of Anthropic, built for onboarding practice. Every person, channel, and rule here is invented.

docs.title: Welcome to the Claude iOS team
docs.body:
You are joining the Claude iOS team. We build the Claude app for iPhone and iPad. Marcus Oyelaran leads the team from San Francisco. Lena Fischer is your teammate, remote in London. Your buddy for the first month is Kai Nakamura on the Claude Web team.
We are spread across San Francisco, New York, London, Dublin, Zurich, and Tokyo, so most of the team is remote to someone. Three habits we care about: Ship small, Say it in writing, Leave the campsite cleaner.
New hires spend week one on the Quest. Every stop was written by someone who was new once too.

docs.title: Teams and who owns what
docs.body:
Claude iOS owns the Claude app for iPhone and iPad. Lead: Marcus Oyelaran. Channel: #claude-ios.
Claude Web owns claude.ai in the browser. Lead: Sofia Reyes. Channel: #claude-web.
Subscriptions owns Claude Pro billing, App Store receipts, and refunds. Lead: Priya Nair. Channel: #subscriptions.
Claude Design owns the design system and app UI. Jun Park is the designer for iOS. Channel: #claude-design.
IT & Devices owns laptops, VPN, and Apple Developer seats. Lead: Dev Patel. Channel: #help-it.
Reliability owns on call, paging (Beacon), and the SEV process. Lead: Nadia Haddad. Channel: #reliability.
People runs onboarding and the buddy program. Lead: Amara Okafor. Channel: #people.
If you do not know who owns something, ask in #where-does-this-live. Nobody minds.

docs.title: Laptops, access, Xcode, and IT
docs.body:
For any laptop, VPN, or access problem post in #help-it. IT & Devices watches it 9am to 6pm Pacific. Include three things: your laptop asset tag (a sticker on the bottom, starts with ANT-), what you tried, and the exact error text. Urgent and blocking? Start your message with BLOCKED. IT opens a ticket for you.
Apple Developer team invites do not come from IT. Your team lead (Marcus) sends the invite from App Store Connect. TestFlight access follows the invite within the hour. Signing certificates are fetched by Xcode once you are on the VPN and in the Apple team.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.body:
TF build: the nightly TestFlight build of the Claude iOS app. It goes out at 6am Pacific to the internal group.
Release train: the weekly App Store submission. It leaves every Tuesday at noon Pacific. Miss it and your change waits a week.
Crash-free rate: the share of sessions with no crash. We watch it every morning. Below 99.5% is a conversation.
Pro: the Claude Pro subscription. Subscriptions team owns billing for it.
Beacon: our paging system. If Beacon calls you, you are on call.
Campsite rule: leave any code or doc you touch a little cleaner than you found it.

docs.title: How we ship the iOS app
docs.body:
1. Make a branch from main. Name it your-name/short-description.
2. Keep the PR small. Under 200 lines is the goal. Split it if it grows.
3. Open the PR with a one paragraph description that says why, not just what. UI changes need a before and after screenshot in the PR.
4. Ask one reviewer. Not two. One. Post the link in #claude-ios.
5. Xcode Cloud must be green. No exceptions, even for typos.
6. Squash merge. The reviewer merges, not the author.
Your first PR should be tiny on purpose. A string typo counts. It teaches you the flow.

docs.title: On call and Beacon
docs.body:
Claude iOS runs a weekly on call rotation through Beacon. Severity levels: SEV1 means users cannot open the app or sign in. SEV2 means a core flow is failing for a slice of users, or crash-free dropped sharply. SEV3 means it can wait until morning.
When Beacon pages you: acknowledge the page within 10 minutes so it does not escalate. Open the runbook linked in the page. If you have not fixed it or found the cause in 30 minutes, escalate to the on call lead. Never sit alone with a SEV1 or SEV2. Asking for help is the rule, not a weakness.
New hires shadow on call for the first month and are never paged alone.

docs.title: Meetings and remote norms
docs.body:
We are spread across six offices and many homes. Every meeting has a written agenda before it starts, or it gets cancelled. Default length is 25 minutes. Wednesdays have no meetings.
On calls: cameras are optional. If you want to speak and cannot find a gap, type 'hand' in the meeting's Slack thread. The host reads the thread queue in order before taking new speakers. This is so remote people on laggy or noisy connections get the same air time.
Decisions made in a meeting are written in the thread within the hour. If it is not written, it did not happen.

docs.title: Coffee chats and the buddy program
docs.body:
Every new hire gets a buddy from a different team. Your buddy is not your manager. Ask them the questions you feel silly asking.
In week one, book at least one coffee chat with someone outside your own team. Use the #coffee-roulette channel or just DM them. People say yes. It is a 20 minute call, no agenda.
Remote inclusion norm: when the office folks grab coffee, someone posts in #hallway so remote people can join by video. Nobody should learn about a decision because they missed the kitchen.
